entry.title: Orientation and external shading relationship

construction.supports: Compose supported roof overhangs and independently editable screens outside actual openings.
construction.materials: Select available finishes after local exposure review.
construction.unsupported: No thermal simulation, movable louvre mechanism or certified energy performance.

entry.when: Hot humid residential envelopes, subject to local sun paths, climate and exposure review.
entry.combinations: Combine with reviewed facade, roof and outdoor-living guidance.
entry.placement: Place shading outside glazing; retain usable covered outdoor space and avoid obstructing breezes. Consider additional vertical shade for low-angle exposure.
entry.principles: Coordinate external shade with opening orientation and climate; a uniform roof projection does not address every sun angle.
entry.capabilities: Australian guidance needs local latitude and seasonal adaptation. Exact shade dimensions, Caribbean performance and site wind conditions are unverified; do not copy Australian north-facing rules.

sources.note: Your Home: Shading; researched 2026-10-28T12:00:00.000Z; published unknown; full-page-observation: Professional guidance relates shading to climate and orientation, discusses low-angle sun, and recommends shaded outdoor areas without blocking breezes in hot humid climates.
